terms.gloss: lay (of a hen), with no object
evidence: Varr. RR 3.9: cum peperērunt, tollere substrāmen
Col. 8.5.1: Cōnfectā brūmā parere ferē id genus avium cōnsuēvit.
terms.comment: The farm writers say of hens simply that they lay, pariunt, without ōva.

evidence: Col. 8.5.1: circā Kalendās Jānuāriās ōva ēdere incipiunt

phrases.english: Have the hens laid? Go and collect the eggs.

phrases.latin: In cubīlibus, cum parturient, acus substernendum; cum peperērunt, tollere substrāmen et recēns aliud subjicere
phrases.english: When they are about to lay, chaff must be spread in the nests; when they have laid, take out the bedding and put in fresh

phrases.latin: Adsiduus autem dēbet esse custōs et speculārī parientēs, quod sē facere gallīnae testantur crēbrīs singultibus interjectā vōce acūtā.
phrases.english: The keeper must be always at hand and watch for the hens laying, which they announce with repeated clucks and a shrill cry between them.

phrases.latin: Observāre itaque dum ēdant ōva et cōnfestim circumīre oportēbit cubīlia, ut quae nāta sunt recolligantur
phrases.english: So he must watch while they lay, and go round the nests at once, to collect the eggs that have been laid

sources: Lewis & Short: pario · Lewis & Short: edo · Lewis & Short: recolligo
John C. Traupman, Conversational Latin for Oral Proficiency, pp. 142, 338.
